title: Deconstructing the Neurobiology of Addiction: Tolerance, Craving & VTA Hijacking
description: Analyze the neurochemical progression from initial recreational drug intake to compulsive habit formation and relapse vulnerability.
problemStatement:
A substance use disorder researcher traces the neurobiological trajectory of cocaine addiction in animal and human models.

### Your Mission:
1. **Acute Pharmacodynamics**: Explain how cocaine blocks the Dopamine Transporter (DAT), elevating extracellular dopamine in the Nucleus Accumbens shell.
2. **Neuroadaptation & Tolerance**: Describe the postsynaptic D2 receptor downregulation and cyclic AMP response element-binding protein (CREB) activation that produces hedonic tolerance (anhedonia to natural rewards).
3. **The Ventral-to-Dorsal Striatal Shift**: Explain how compulsive drug-seeking transitions from ventral striatal goal-directed action (VTA $\rightarrow$ NAc) to dorsal striatal automatic stimulus-response habit execution (substantia nigra $\rightarrow$ putamen), and identify the role of the prefrontal cortex in craving relapse.
hints: Hint 1: DAT blockade prevents presynaptic dopamine reuptake, resulting in continuous stimulation of postsynaptic receptors.
Hint 2: As addiction progresses, behavioral control shifts from voluntary reward pursuit to compulsive, inflexible habit loops mediated by the dorsal striatum.
